links.comparator_used: Standard GPT-4o (no retrieval) vs RAG-LLM using a knowledge base of international consensus reports and clinical treatment guides, on 40 vignettes processed twice each (160 plans)
links.outcome: Expert-rated clinical accuracy overall, plus domain scores for evidence traceability, citation precision and biomechanical spatial planning
links.effect: Overall clinical accuracy: no significant difference (P = 0.642). Evidence traceability and citation precision: RAG-LLM significantly better (P = 0.046). Biomechanical spatial planning: standard LLM better (P = 0.025). Neither model showed severe literature fabrication.
links.tradeoff: RAG showed 'retrieval bias' in soft-tissue complication scenarios, leading to inappropriate hard-tissue augmentation (overtreatment). Its advantage diminished in out-of-distribution synthetic cases lacking thematic overlap with the knowledge base. Continuous expert oversight is still needed.
links.quote: However, domain-specific analysis revealed that the RAG-LLM significantly outperformed the standard model in evidence traceability and citation precision (P = 0.046).

design_hint: retrieval grounding added to an existing LLM
